questions.q: Which act was the first step taken by the British Government to control and regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India?
questions.why: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first parliamentary intervention to control the Company, marking the beginning of central administration in India.

questions.q: Under the Regulating Act of 1773, the Governor of Bengal was designated as the Governor-General of Bengal. Who was the first person to hold this title?
questions.why: Lord Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal, centralizing power by making the governors of Bombay and Madras subordinate to him.

questions.q: The Supreme Court at Calcutta was established under which of the following acts?
questions.why: The Act provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774) comprising one chief justice and three other judges.

questions.q: Who was appointed as the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court established at Calcutta in 1774?
questions.why: Sir Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta, established under the 1773 Act.

questions.q: Which act prohibited the servants of the East India Company from engaging in any private trade or accepting bribes from the 'natives'?
questions.why: To curb massive corruption, the Regulating Act of 1773 strictly prohibited Company servants from private trading and accepting presents or bribes.

questions.q: Which act was passed by the British Parliament primarily to rectify the defects of the Regulating Act of 1773?
questions.why: The Amending Act of 1781, also known as the Act of Settlement, was passed to fix the jurisdictional clashes between the Supreme Court and the Governor-General's Council.

questions.q: The Amending Act of 1781 exempted which of the following from the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court at Calcutta?
questions.why: The Act of 1781 exempted the Governor-General and the Council from the Supreme Court's jurisdiction for acts done in their official capacity.

questions.q: Which act distinguished between the commercial and political functions of the East India Company for the first time?
questions.why: Pitt's India Act created a system of double government by separating commercial functions (Court of Directors) from political functions (Board of Control).

questions.q: Under Pitt's India Act of 1784, a new body was created to manage political affairs. What was it called?
questions.why: The Board of Control was a newly created body comprising British cabinet ministers to oversee and direct all political, civil, and military affairs in India.

questions.q: For the first time, the Company's territories in India were called the 'British possessions in India' under which act?
questions.why: Pitt's India Act is highly significant because it was the first time Indian territories were officially claimed as British possessions by the Crown.

questions.q: Which act gave the Governor-General the power to override his council's decision under special circumstances?
questions.why: Lord Cornwallis demanded the power to override his council and the position of Commander-in-Chief, which were granted via the Act of 1786.

questions.q: The Charter Act of 1793 provided that the salaries of the members of the Board of Control would be paid from:
opts: The personal funds of the Monarch
questions.why: This act mandated that the salaries and expenses of the Board of Control and their staff were to be charged directly to the Indian revenues.

questions.q: Which act abolished the trade monopoly of the East India Company in India, throwing trade open to all British subjects?
questions.why: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's monopoly over trade in India due to pressure from British merchants, though it retained the monopoly on tea and trade with China.

questions.q: The Charter Act of 1813 allowed which group to come to India for the purpose of 'enlightening' the people?
questions.why: The act officially permitted Christian missionaries to enter India to promote religious and moral improvements among the local populace.

questions.q: Which act provided an annual sum of one lakh rupees for the promotion of literature and education among Indians?
questions.why: This was a landmark step where the British Parliament officially allocated 100,000 rupees annually for the revival of literature and the promotion of sciences in India.

questions.q: Which act was the final step towards the centralization of administration in British India?
questions.why: The Charter Act of 1833 represented the peak of centralization by making the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India with all civil and military powers.

questions.q: Under the Charter Act of 1833, who became the first Governor-General of India?
questions.why: Lord William Bentinck was elevated from Governor-General of Bengal to the first Governor-General of India, gaining exclusive legislative powers for the entire country.

questions.q: The Charter Act of 1833 completely ended the East India Company's monopoly in which trade sectors?
questions.why: While the 1813 act ended general monopoly, the 1833 act completely ended the Company's commercial activities, including its remaining monopoly on tea and China trade.

questions.q: Which act made a failed attempt to introduce a system of open competition for the selection of civil servants in India?
questions.why: The 1833 act attempted to allow Indians into the civil service, but the provision was heavily opposed and negated by the Court of Directors.

questions.q: The first Law Commission of India was established under the Charter Act of 1833. Who was its chairman?
questions.why: Lord Macaulay chaired the first Law Commission, which was tasked with consolidating and codifying Indian laws and penal codes.

questions.q: Which act separated, for the first time, the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's council?
questions.why: The 1853 act established a separate six-member 'Legislative Council', functioning as a mini-Parliament, distinct from the executive functions.

questions.q: The Charter Act of 1853 introduced an open competition system for civil services. Which committee was appointed in 1854 to implement this?
questions.why: The Macaulay Committee (the Committee on the Indian Civil Service) was appointed in 1854 to formally open covenanted civil services to Indians.

questions.q: Which act introduced local representation in the Indian (Central) Legislative Council for the first time?
questions.why: Out of the six new legislative members of the governor-general's council, four were appointed by the local governments of Madras, Bombay, Bengal, and Agra.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1858 was passed in the immediate aftermath of which historical event?
questions.why: The Revolt of 1857 (Sepoy Mutiny) exposed the severe flaws of Company rule, prompting the British Crown to assume direct control over India.

questions.q: Under the Government of India Act 1858, the title of Governor-General of India was changed to:
questions.why: The title was changed to Viceroy, making him the direct representative of the British Crown in India. Lord Canning became the first Viceroy.

questions.q: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
questions.why: Lord Canning, who was the Governor-General during the 1857 revolt, was appointed as the first Viceroy of India under the 1858 Act.

questions.q: Which act completely abolished the 'Double Government' system of the Board of Control and Court of Directors?
questions.why: The 1858 Act ended Pitt's double government system and transferred all powers of government, territories, and revenues directly to the British Crown.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1858 created a new office with absolute authority and control over Indian administration known as:
questions.why: The Secretary of State for India, a member of the British Cabinet, was vested with complete authority and control over Indian administration.

questions.q: To assist the Secretary of State for India, the Act of 1858 established a council of how many members?
questions.why: A 15-member advisory body, known as the Council of India, was established to assist the Secretary of State, who served as its chairman.

questions.q: Which act marks the beginning of representative institutions by associating Indians with the law-making process?
questions.why: The 1861 Act allowed the Viceroy to nominate some Indians as non-official members of his expanded legislative council, initiating representative elements.

questions.q: In 1862, Lord Canning nominated three Indians to his legislative council. Which of the following was NOT one of them?
questions.why: Lord Canning nominated the Raja of Benares, the Maharaja of Patiala, and Sir Dinkar Rao. Dadabhai Naoroji was not among these initial three.

questions.q: Which act reversed the centralizing tendency that started with the Regulating Act of 1773?
questions.why: The 1861 Act restored legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies, initiating the process of administrative decentralization.

questions.q: The 'Portfolio System', introduced by Lord Canning in 1859, was given statutory recognition by which act?
questions.why: The 1861 Act officially recognized the Portfolio System, where each member of the Viceroy's council was placed in charge of specific government departments.

questions.q: Which act empowered the Viceroy to issue ordinances without the concurrence of the legislative council during an emergency?
questions.why: The Viceroy was given the power to issue ordinances that had the same force as acts, with a maximum life of six months during emergencies.

questions.q: Which act increased the number of additional (non-official) members in the Central and provincial legislative councils, but maintained the official majority?
questions.why: The 1892 Act expanded the legislative councils and introduced a limited, indirect provision for the use of elections to fill non-official seats.

questions.q: The power to discuss the budget and address questions to the executive was first given to the legislative councils under which act?
questions.why: The Indian Councils Act 1892 enlarged the functions of the legislative councils, granting them the crucial right to discuss the annual financial statement (budget).

questions.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is also commonly known as:
questions.why: It is named after the Secretary of State for India, Lord Morley, and the Viceroy of India, Lord Minto, who drafted these structural reforms.

questions.q: Which act introduced a system of communal representation for Muslims by accepting the concept of a 'separate electorate'?
questions.why: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 legalized communalism by providing separate electorates, where Muslim members were elected exclusively by Muslim voters.

questions.q: Who is known as the 'Father of Communal Electorate' in India?
questions.why: Due to his role in implementing separate electorates for Muslims in the 1909 Act, Viceroy Lord Minto is regarded as the father of communal electorates.

questions.q: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 provided for the association of Indians with the executive councils for the first time. Who was the first Indian to join the Viceroy's Executive Council?
questions.why: Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the first Indian to join the Viceroy's Executive Council, being appointed strictly as the Law Member.

questions.q: Under the Indian Councils Act of 1909, members of the legislative council were allowed to ask supplementary questions. True or False?
questions.why: The 1909 Act further enlarged the deliberative functions, allowing members to ask supplementary questions and move resolutions on the budget.

questions.q: Which declaration in 1917 stated that the British policy objective was the gradual development of self-governing institutions in India?
questions.why: On August 20, 1917, Edwin Montagu declared that the British objective was the progressive realization of responsible government in India.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1919 is also known as:
questions.why: It was named after Edwin Montagu (Secretary of State) and Lord Chelmsford (Viceroy), who framed the structural changes for provincial autonomy.

questions.q: Which act introduced the system of 'Dyarchy' (dual rule) in the provinces?
questions.why: The 1919 Act divided provincial subjects into two parts: transferred subjects (administered by governor with ministers) and reserved subjects (governor with executive council).

questions.q: Under the Dyarchy system introduced in 1919, 'Reserved Subjects' were administered by:
opts: The Governor with the aid of ministers
The Governor and his executive council
questions.ansText: The Governor and his executive council
questions.why: Reserved subjects (like police, justice, revenue) were kept under the absolute control of the Governor and his non-responsible executive council.

questions.q: Which act introduced, for the first time, bicameralism and direct elections in the country?
questions.why: The 1919 Act replaced the Indian Legislative Council with a bicameral legislature consisting of an Upper House (Council of State) and a Lower House (Legislative Assembly).

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1919 extended the principle of communal representation by providing separate electorates for which new groups?
opts: Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans
questions.ansText: Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans
questions.why: While the 1909 act gave separate electorates to Muslims, the 1919 act broadened this divisive policy to include Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans.

questions.q: Which act mandated that three of the six members of the Viceroy's Executive Council were to be Indian (excluding the Commander-in-Chief)?
questions.why: To increase Indian participation at the highest executive level, the 1919 Act reserved half the seats (3 out of 6) in the Viceroy's council for Indians.

questions.q: The provision for the establishment of a Public Service Commission in India was made by which act?
questions.why: The 1919 Act provided for a Public Service Commission. Subsequently, the Central Public Service Commission was set up in 1926 to recruit civil servants.

questions.q: Which act separated provincial budgets from the Central budget for the first time?
questions.why: To grant financial autonomy, the 1919 Act separated provincial budgets from the central budget and authorized provincial legislatures to enact their own budgets.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1919 provided for the appointment of a statutory commission to inquire into its working after how many years?
questions.why: The act mandated a statutory commission after 10 years to assess its impact. This led to the premature appointment of the Simon Commission in 1927.

questions.q: The Simon Commission (Statutory Commission) was appointed in November 1927. How many members did it have?
questions.why: The Simon Commission was a seven-member statutory commission consisting entirely of British members, which caused mass boycotts by all Indian parties.

questions.q: Who was the Prime Minister of Britain who announced the 'Communal Award' in August 1932?
questions.why: Ramsay MacDonald announced a scheme of representation for minorities known as the Communal Award, which highly controversially extended separate electorates to the depressed classes.

questions.q: The Poona Pact of 1932 was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and:
questions.why: To protest the Communal Award, Gandhi fasted until a pact was signed with Dr. Ambedkar, retaining joint electorates but reserving seats for the depressed classes.

questions.q: Which act was the second milestone towards a completely responsible government in India, being a lengthy document of 321 sections and 10 schedules?
questions.why: The 1935 Act was a massive piece of legislation that served as the primary blueprint for the modern Constitution of India.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1935 provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation consisting of:
opts: Provinces and Princely States as units
questions.ansText: Provinces and Princely States as units
questions.why: The act aimed to unite British Indian provinces and Princely States into a federation, though it never materialized as the states refused to join.

questions.q: Under the Government of India Act 1935, legislative powers were divided between the Centre and units into how many lists?
questions.why: The 1935 Act introduced the three-list system—Federal List, Provincial List, and Concurrent List—which later heavily influenced the 7th Schedule of the Constitution.

questions.q: Under the Government of India Act 1935, the residuary powers were vested in the:
questions.why: Unlike the modern Constitution where residuary powers lie with the Centre, the 1935 Act explicitly gave all residuary legislative powers to the Viceroy.

questions.q: Which act abolished 'Dyarchy' in the provinces and introduced 'Provincial Autonomy' in its place?
questions.why: The 1935 Act ended the flawed dual-rule of Dyarchy in provinces, allowing provincial governments to act autonomously within their defined spheres.

questions.q: While abolishing it in provinces, the Government of India Act 1935 provided for the adoption of 'Dyarchy' at which level?
questions.why: The Act shifted Dyarchy to the Centre, dividing federal subjects into reserved and transferred subjects, though this provision never came into operation.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1935 introduced bicameralism in how many out of the eleven British Indian provinces?
questions.why: Bicameralism was introduced in six provinces: Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam, and the United Provinces.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1935 extended the principle of separate electorates to which new groups?
opts: Depressed classes (scheduled castes), women, and labor
questions.ansText: Depressed classes (scheduled castes), women, and labor
questions.why: The British continued their divide-and-rule policy by extending separate electorates further to scheduled castes, women, and the working class.

questions.q: Which act abolished the Council of India, which was previously established by the Government of India Act of 1858?
questions.why: The 1935 Act dissolved the 15-member advisory Council of India in London, replacing it with a team of advisors for the Secretary of State.

questions.q: The establishment of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was provided for under which act?
questions.why: To control the currency and credit of the nation, the 1935 Act explicitly provided for the creation of the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1935 provided for the establishment of which of the following commissions?
opts: Federal, Provincial, and Joint Public Service Commissions
questions.ansText: Federal, Provincial, and Joint Public Service Commissions
questions.why: Expanding on the 1919 act, the 1935 act allowed for public service commissions at the federal level, provincial level, and joint commissions for two or more provinces.

questions.q: The Federal Court of India, established in 1937, was set up under the provisions of which act?
questions.why: The 1935 Act provided for a Federal Court to resolve disputes between the center and provinces, which later became the precursor to the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Which British Prime Minister declared on February 20, 1947, that British rule in India would end by June 30, 1948?
questions.why: Clement Attlee made this historic declaration, stating that power would be transferred to responsible Indian hands no later than June 1948.

questions.q: In response to the Muslim League's demand for partition, the British government put forth a partition plan on June 3, 1947. What is it famously called?
questions.why: Lord Mountbatten formulated the partition plan of June 3, 1947, which was reluctantly accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League.

questions.q: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 ended British rule and declared India an independent and sovereign state from which exact date?
questions.why: The act formalized the Mountbatten Plan, establishing the independent dominions of India and Pakistan effective midnight of August 14-15, 1947.

questions.q: Which act officially abolished the office of the Viceroy of India and provided for a Governor-General for each dominion?
questions.why: The 1947 Act removed the title of Viceroy and reverted to Governor-General, who was now a constitutional head appointed on the advice of the dominion cabinet.

questions.q: Who became the first Governor-General of the new Dominion of India in 1947?
questions.why: Lord Mountbatten remained in India temporarily after independence as the first Governor-General of the newly independent Indian dominion.

questions.q: Who was the first (and only) Indian to hold the post of Governor-General of independent India?
questions.why: Chakravarti Rajagopalachari succeeded Lord Mountbatten to become the first and last Indian Governor-General before the post was abolished in 1950.

questions.q: The Indian Independence Act 1947 abolished the office of the Secretary of State for India. His functions were transferred to the:
opts: Secretary of State for Commonwealth Affairs
questions.ansText: Secretary of State for Commonwealth Affairs
questions.why: With India gaining dominion status, the absolute powers of the Secretary of State were dismantled and residual functions shifted to Commonwealth affairs.

questions.q: Under the Indian Independence Act 1947, who was granted the absolute right to frame and adopt any constitution for their respective nations?
opts: The Constituent Assemblies of the two dominions
questions.ansText: The Constituent Assemblies of the two dominions
questions.why: The act empowered the Constituent Assemblies of both India and Pakistan to frame their constitutions and repeal any prior British acts.

questions.q: The Indian Independence Act 1947 proclaimed the lapse of British paramountcy over:
questions.why: The act legally ended all treaties and paramountcy the British Crown held over the princely states, leaving them free to join India, Pakistan, or remain independent.

questions.q: Which act dropped the title of 'Emperor of India' from the royal titles of the King of England?
questions.why: As a direct consequence of declaring India completely sovereign, the British monarch was stripped of the 'Emperor of India' title.

questions.q: Until the new Constitution was drafted, the governance of India and Pakistan was directed to be carried on in accordance with which act?
questions.why: The 1947 Act stipulated that until new constitutions were adopted, both dominions would be governed under the framework of the Government of India Act 1935.

questions.q: Which act discontinued the appointment to civil services and reservation of posts by the Secretary of State for India?
questions.why: The 1947 act stopped the recruitment of civil servants from London, though existing civil servants retained their prior benefits.

questions.q: Which act designated the Governor-General of India and the provincial governors as mere 'constitutional (nominal) heads' of the states?
questions.why: With the transfer of real power to democratically elected ministers, the Governor-General and provincial governors were reduced to nominal figureheads.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Regulating Act of 1773: (I) It prohibited private trade by company servants. (II) It created a Supreme Court at Calcutta. (III) It established the Board of Control. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement III is incorrect. The Board of Control was established later by Pitt's India Act of 1784, not the 1773 Act.

questions.q: Consider the following about Pitt's India Act 1784: (I) It separated the commercial and political functions of the Company. (II) It made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement II is incorrect. The elevation to Governor-General of India occurred much later under the Charter Act of 1833.

questions.q: Consider the following about the Charter Act of 1833: (I) It ended the Company's monopoly in the tea trade. (II) It attempted to introduce open competition for civil services. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: Both are correct. It completely destroyed the commercial monopoly (including tea) and made a failed attempt to allow Indians into the civil service.

questions.q: Consider the following: (I) The portfolio system was introduced by Lord Canning. (II) The Indian Councils Act 1861 recognized the portfolio system. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: Lord Canning introduced the portfolio system in 1859, and it was legally legitimized by the Indian Councils Act of 1861.

questions.q: Consider the following about the Act of 1892: (I) It introduced direct elections for the first time. (II) It gave the legislative council the power to discuss the budget. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement I is incorrect. Direct elections were introduced in 1919; the 1892 act only allowed for limited 'indirect' elections via nomination.

questions.q: Consider the following about the Morley-Minto Reforms (1909): (I) It introduced separate electorates for Muslims. (II) It introduced dyarchy in the provinces. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement II is incorrect. Dyarchy in the provinces was introduced a decade later by the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919.

questions.q: Consider the following features of the Government of India Act 1919: (I) Introduction of bicameralism at the centre. (II) Separation of provincial budgets from the central budget. (III) Abolition of the Board of Control. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement III is incorrect. The Board of Control was abolished much earlier by the Government of India Act of 1858.

questions.q: Consider the following about the Government of India Act 1935: (I) It abolished dyarchy in provinces. (II) It introduced dyarchy at the Centre. (III) It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: All statements are correct. The 1935 Act was a massive structural overhaul that shifted dyarchy to the center and established the Federal Court.

questions.q: Arrange the following in chronological order: (1) Pitt's India Act (2) Act of Settlement (3) Regulating Act (4) Charter Act ending tea monopoly.
questions.why: The correct order is Regulating Act (1773), Act of Settlement (1781), Pitt's India Act (1784), and the Charter Act ending tea monopoly (1833).

questions.q: Arrange the following in chronological order: (1) Morley-Minto Reforms (2) Simon Commission (3) Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (4) Communal Award.
questions.why: The chronological order is Morley-Minto (1909), Montagu-Chelmsford (1919), Simon Commission (1927), and the Communal Award (1932).

questions.q: Arrange the following in chronological order: (1) Cabinet Mission (2) August Offer (3) Mountbatten Plan (4) Cripps Mission.
questions.why: The correct historical timeline is August Offer (1940), Cripps Mission (1942), Cabinet Mission (1946), and the Mountbatten Plan (1947).

questions.q: Which of the following acts was described by Jawaharlal Nehru as a 'machine with strong brakes but no engine'?
questions.why: Nehru strongly criticized the 1935 Act because despite its federal structure, absolute veto powers remained concentrated in the hands of the British authorities.

questions.q: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the trade monopoly of the East India Company in India for another period of how many years?
questions.why: Following the tradition of periodic charter renewals, the 1793 act guaranteed the Company's trade monopoly in India for an additional 20 years.

questions.q: Under which act were the laws made by the Governor-General's council first called 'Acts' rather than 'Regulations'?
questions.why: The 1833 act centralized legislative powers; laws made prior to this were called Regulations, while laws made under this act were termed 'Acts'.

questions.q: The Charter Act of 1853 reduced the number of members of the Court of Directors from 24 to:
questions.why: The act reduced the Court of Directors' strength to 18, out of which 6 were to be directly nominated by the British Crown.

questions.q: Which act made a statutory provision that Indian revenues could not be used for military operations outside India without Parliamentary consent?
questions.why: To prevent the exploitation of Indian resources for British imperial wars, the 1858 Act mandated Parliament's approval for external military funding.

questions.q: Under the Government of India Act 1858, the Secretary of State for India was responsible directly to:
questions.why: As a member of the British cabinet, the Secretary of State was ultimately responsible to the British Parliament for all Indian affairs.

questions.q: The Indian Councils Act 1861 created new legislative councils for which three provinces?
questions.why: The decentralization policy of 1861 led to the establishment of new legislative councils for Bengal (1862), NWFP (1886), and Punjab (1897).

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1919 came into actual administrative force in which year?
questions.why: Although passed in 1919, the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms and the new constitutional structures only came into active operation in 1921.

questions.q: Under the Government of India Act 1919, who was given the power to enact a budget for the country even if the legislature refused to pass it?
questions.why: Despite the new bicameral legislature, the Viceroy retained absolute certification powers to enact bills and pass the budget independently if necessary.

questions.q: The Indian Franchise Committee (Lothian Committee) was appointed in connection with which major British policy?
questions.why: The Lothian Committee's recommendations on expanding the electorate directly formed the statistical basis for Ramsay MacDonald's Communal Award in 1932.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1935 abolished the system of provincial dyarchy which had been operational for how many years?
questions.why: Provincial dyarchy was introduced by the 1919 Act (operational from 1921) and abolished by the 1935 Act (operational from 1937), making it a 16-year run.

questions.q: Which political leader famously described the Government of India Act 1935 as 'thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable'?
questions.why: M.A. Jinnah harshly rejected the federal scheme of the 1935 Act, primarily because it didn't align with the political ambitions of the Muslim League at the time.

questions.q: The Indian Independence Act 1947 received the royal assent from the British monarch on which date?
questions.why: The Independence Bill was introduced in the British Parliament on July 4 and swiftly received royal assent on July 18, 1947, sealing India's fate.

questions.q: Under the Indian Independence Act 1947, the Constituent Assembly of India also functioned as the:
questions.why: Until the first general elections could be held, the Constituent Assembly doubled as India's first provisional Parliament, performing legislative duties.

questions.q: Which British official was responsible for drawing the boundaries between India and Pakistan following the 1947 Act?
questions.why: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the Boundary Commissions tasked with drawing the borders of Punjab and Bengal, leading to the infamous Radcliffe Line.

questions.q: Consider the following: (I) The 1833 Act created the Law Commission. (II) The 1853 Act created a separate Legislative Council. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: Both are true. Macaulay headed the first Law Commission (1833), and the 1853 Act separated executive and legislative council functions.

questions.q: Consider the following about the 1919 Act: (I) It introduced direct elections. (II) It established the Reserve Bank of India. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: Statement II is incorrect. The Reserve Bank of India was conceptualized and legally provided for under the later Government of India Act of 1935.

questions.q: Consider the following about the 1935 Act: (I) It extended the franchise to about 10% of the total population. (II) It separated Burma from India. Which is/are correct?
questions.why: Both statements are accurate facts. The 1935 act expanded voting rights slightly and legally detached the administration of Burma from British India.

questions.q: Arrange the following Governors-General/Viceroys in chronological order of their administrative acts: (1) William Bentinck (2) Canning (3) Warren Hastings (4) Minto.
questions.why: Warren Hastings (1773 Act), William Bentinck (1833 Act), Canning (1858 Act), and Minto (1909 Act).

questions.q: Which act officially recognized the principle of election for the first time, although the word 'election' was not explicitly used in the text?
questions.why: The 1892 act allowed certain bodies to 'recommend' members for nomination to the councils, which was a de facto system of indirect elections.

questions.q: The provision for appointing an Indian to the Viceroy's Executive Council was originally introduced by which act?
questions.why: The Morley-Minto reforms of 1909 broke the all-British executive barrier, leading to the appointment of Satyendra Prasad Sinha.

questions.q: Under the Government of India Act 1919, 'Transferred Subjects' were administered by the Governor with the aid of:
opts: Ministers responsible to the legislative council
questions.ansText: Ministers responsible to the legislative council
questions.why: Under Dyarchy, transferred subjects (like health and education) were managed by the Governor acting on the advice of democratically elected ministers.

questions.q: The Simon Commission recommended the abolition of which specific administrative system?
questions.why: The Simon Commission reported that Dyarchy was a failure and recommended replacing it entirely with provincial autonomy, which happened in 1935.

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Simon Commission?
opts: Establishment of a federation of British India and princely states
questions.why: The Simon Commission controversially recommended the continuation of communal electorates, which was a major point of contention for Indian leaders.

questions.q: To consider the proposals of the Simon Commission, the British Government convened three Round Table Conferences in which city?
questions.why: Between 1930 and 1932, the British hosted three Round Table Conferences in London to discuss future constitutional reforms for India.

questions.q: The White Paper on Constitutional Reforms, drafted after the Round Table Conferences, was submitted to a Joint Select Committee headed by:
questions.why: The Joint Select Committee, chaired by Lord Linlithgow, reviewed the White Paper and eventually drafted the Government of India Bill (1935 Act).

questions.q: Which act introduced the instrument of instructions for the Governor-General and Governors, which later influenced the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.why: The 'Instrument of Instructions' issued under the 1935 Act served as a direct template for the Directive Principles in the 1950 Constitution.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1935 divided federal subjects into 'Reserved' and 'Transferred'. Which of the following was a 'Reserved' subject?
questions.why: Critical subjects like Defense, External Affairs, Ecclesiastical Affairs, and Tribal Areas were strictly reserved for the Governor-General under the proposed federal dyarchy.

questions.q: The Government of India Act 1935 provided for the establishment of a Federal Railway Authority. How many members were to be in this authority?
questions.why: To keep railway administration free from political interference, the 1935 Act created a 7-member statutory Federal Railway Authority.

questions.q: Which British act declared that the paramountcy of the British Crown over Indian princely states would technically lapse on the day of independence?
questions.why: The 1947 Act legally severed all treaties, returning full sovereignty to the princely states, forcing them to decide their own political future.

questions.q: Under the Indian Independence Act 1947, the Governor-General was to be appointed by the British King on the advice of:
questions.why: After independence, the British King lost unilateral appointment power; he could only appoint the Governor-General based strictly on the respective Dominion Cabinet's advice.
